messages.text:
Hi Luis,

Introducing Rupert Ashdown, who owns Merefurrow Farm near Faversham. I was at a wedding there in September and spent most of the evening talking to him about his website, which he describes as "a brochure that answers the phone badly". He wants a site that takes enquiries for retreats and small weddings properly.

Rupert, Luis leads product design at Acme and is far better at this than I am at ceilidh dancing.

Z

Zainab Bello
Content Designer, Acme Studio
acme.example

Dear Luis,

It is good of you to look at this, and thank you, Zainab, for the introduction and for the dancing, which was braver than you make out.

The farm has a converted barn that seats sixty and fourteen bedrooms between the farmhouse and the old dairy. At present every enquiry comes by telephone, and I lose a good many between half past six and nine in the evening, when I am out with the animals and the house is empty. The website was put together by my nephew in 2014; he has since moved to Vancouver and I have not had the heart to touch it.

What I should like is simple enough: people able to see which dates are free, ask for a quotation, and read what we can and cannot do without ringing me. I attach our brochure and a few photographs, so you can see what we are working with.

I should be glad to talk whenever suits you.

With kind regards, Rupert Ashdown

Hi Rupert,

I'll check with Fiona, who handles new work here, and get back to you next week. A site this size might be a better fit for a smaller studio.

The photos are lovely. Separately, the studio is looking for somewhere to take about 38 people for two days this autumn. Do you take groups that size, and roughly what would it cost?

Thanks,
Luis

Luis Cordero
Lead Product Designer, Acme Studio
3rd floor, 48 Turnmill Street, London EC1M 5RR
acme.example

Ha, I was about to suggest the offsite. Tash has been complaining about seaside prices since January.

Z

Zainab Bello
Content Designer, Acme Studio
acme.example

Dear Luis,

We do. For thirty-eight I would put twenty-eight in the farmhouse and the dairy, two to a room, and the other ten at the inn in the village, which is a five-minute walk down the lane. A usual two-day arrangement runs like this:

Day one
10:30 arrival, coffee in the barn
13:00 lunch
19:30 dinner

Day two
08:00 breakfast
12:30 lunch
15:00 departure

For October or November the cost would be in the region of £8,400 for the two days, everything but the wine. I hold a date against a deposit of £2,000.

Do let me know about the website once you have spoken to Fiona. I am in no great hurry, but I should like something better in place before next year's wedding season.

With kind regards, Rupert Ashdown

subject: portfolio for when the junior role opens

messages.text:
Luis - before you disappear to Scotland.

Portfolio from Maja Sobczak, graduated from Camberwell in June, I met her at the degree show. maja-sobczak.example/work, password heron26. Strong on type and editorial, thin on product.

Worth telling her to apply when the junior role opens? Can wait till you’re back.
K.

Hey Kasia,

Yes, tell her to apply. I'd ask her to add a bit about the recipe planner first.

I looked on the train. The editorial work is the best I've seen from a graduate this year. The Southwark zine is lovely: the grid holds up across forty pages and she clearly knows when to break it. The type specimen for her degree show is good too, if a bit long.

The product side is where it falls down. There's one app project, the recipe planner, and it's screens without a problem. I can't tell who it's for, what she tried first, or what she threw away. That's exactly what we'd ask about in an interview, and right now she'd have nothing to say.

She could take one bit of the planner and show how she got there. Even a photo of the first sketch and a few notes from watching someone use it would tell me more than another screen. If she can get that in before the role opens, I'd put her on the shortlist.

I'll write her proper notes when I'm back on the 17th, and we can decide whether they come from you or from me. Probably better from you, since you know her.

Thanks,
Luis

Luis Cordero
Lead Product Designer, Acme Studio
3rd floor, 48 Turnmill Street, London EC1M 5RR
acme.example

Agreed, from me is better. Enjoy the rain.
K.

Love, Felix

subject: Pennywort accessibility audit: what I've decided

messages.text:
Hey Luis,

I’ve kept Pennywort’s tier colours on the badges, which means changing where we use them. Gold was doing the work of a text colour and a label. The badges now say Bronze, Silver or Gold in dark type, with the tier colours behind them. Steve won't love it, but Owen agreed on Wednesday's call, and while Hannah is on leave it's his decision.

The audit came back from Nadia at Clearpath yesterday. 23 findings: 4 blockers, 11 serious, 8 minor. The blockers are:

1. the points balance is an image, so a screen reader says nothing at all
2. the scan button on the till screen is 36 px, under the target size
3. the gold badge text is 2.1:1 on white
4. reward expiry dates only show on hover

All four go into sprint 9, which starts on 5 October. Dev takes 2 and 4 because they're in checkout, which is his now, and I'll do 1 and 3. I've split the serious ones between sprints 9 and 10. The minor ones are in the backlog with an a11y label so they don't vanish.

I’ll bring the revised badges to Monday’s review in case Steve asks to see the gold one.

The full report is in the Pennywort folder as Clearpath_audit_Sept26.pdf. For anything about the points engine, Owen Pratt knows it better than anyone on our side. For the till screens, ask Dev.

Marcus

Marcus Adeyemi
Senior Product Designer, Acme Studio

subject: odd question about May last year

messages.text:
Felix, one more on the deposit, sorry. The two you sent in September are great but the door's mostly behind me and Biscuit. Did you take any others inside the flat that week? The bedroom door in particular. Of the money in dispute, £150 is for scratches Peter says Biscuit made. Biscuit had been with us about a week when you came, so a photo from then would help.

no worries if not
L

Dear Luis,

I am at the kitchen table with the radiator making its October noise, a sort of knocking, as if someone small were trapped inside and too polite to shout.

I dug out the old laptop. It still has the sticker you put over the camera. I did take photographs at Albion Road, mostly of the risograph proofs drying on your kitchen table, because I was proud of them and wanted Lotte to see. In one, from the morning of 16 May, the bedroom door is open behind the table and you can see the handle and the panel above it quite clearly. There are marks just above the handle, two or three, pale. I would not call them scratches. They look like something was dragged past the door rather than at it.

I have put that photograph and the two either side of it in the old album from my visit, albums.paperkite.example/felix-london-25, so you can see them full size. The date is in the files, if that is the kind of thing a deposit scheme cares about.

I am sorry this is still going on. When we left our flat in Kreuzberg the landlord tried to charge us for the sun fading the floorboards, so I believe you completely about landlords.

Love, Felix

this is perfect. the marks are exactly where they are now, same size. Niamh says thank you and also asks who the man in the kettle is (it's you).

can we send it to the deposit scheme with your name as the person who took it?
L

Dear Luis,

Lotte has a cold and has decided the only cure is a story about a cat who scratches doors, so you are now famous in Neukolln.

Of course you can use my name, and my address if they want it. I still won't write about the door from memory, as I said in September, but this much I can do: a short note saying when I took the photograph and that the marks are in it. Tell me what it should say and I will sign it in my best handwriting, which is not very good.

Love, Felix

we'll send yours with Niamh's check-in photos. evidence is due Friday the 23rd. Peter turned down the £75 for the door, so we're asking for the whole lot back.

a signed note would be great. two lines is plenty: you stayed 15–19 May 2025, and the marks were there when you took the photo on the 16th. thanks Felix
L

messages.text:
Hi Luis,

I host Small Screens, a fortnightly podcast about the design of everyday software: the apps people use without thinking, and the people who sweat over them. I saw you're on the Margins line-up in December, and the idea of designing for the last 10 metres is exactly the kind of thing our listeners love. Someone also told me you were behind the Kestrel Pay redesign, which I use every month and have never once sworn at.

Would you come on? It's 45 minutes, recorded in person at our studio in Hackney Wick, lightly edited, and you'd see the cut before it goes out. Any of these would work for us:

- Tuesday 10 November, 10:00
- Thursday 19 November, 14:00
- any morning in the week of 7 December

No fee, I'm afraid, but there's good coffee and a canal outside.

Cheers,

Theo Marchetti
Host, Small Screens - conversations about the design of everyday software
